Diagrammatic Reasoning, Formally
Damien Pous # Ñ
CNRS, LIP, ENS de Lyon, France

      Abstract
Modern proof assistants make it possible to verify theorems, but often makes it harder than with
pen and paper. This is especially true in domains where proofs are best depicted using diagrams.
For instance, confluence diagrams in rewriting theory, commuting diagrams in category theory, or
string diagrams in monoidal categories. By using various tools and techniques to solve well-defined
classes of goals, infer appropriate data, or perform high-level reasoning steps [2, 1], I will show how
to obtain robust and elegant proof scripts in these application domains [3, 4].

2012 ACM Subject Classification Theory of computation → Logic

Keywords and phrases Formal proofs, graphical proofs, string diagrams, monoidal categories, Kleene
algebra, relation algebra, Rocq
